rationale: Indemnity in this Agreement runs one way only: Article XII (p0128-p0129) is a broad Licensee indemnity in favour of Licensor, and there is no Licensor indemnity anywhere (no responsive language in Articles VIII, X, XIII or the General Provisions). Article XIII(a) compounds this by providing that "UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE FOR ANY ACTIONS, CLAIMS OR THE LIKE ... THAT THE USE OF THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY ... MAY RESULT IN ANY INFRINGEMENT", and Article XIII(b) caps Licensor's total liability at one half of amounts paid. That is walk-away territory (no Vendor IP indemnity plus a one-way Customer indemnity), so it fails the fallback. We therefore target the fallback: a Licensor IP indemnity with the customary Customer modification, combination and specification exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, subject to a 3x annual fees super-cap, and we carve that indemnity out of Article XIII(a) and (b) only so far as necessary to keep it effective. We have not sought the preferred-level additions (defence duty, affiliates, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, procedure, narrowing of Licensee's indemnity) in this redline.

verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete: Article XII-A grants an operative Licensor IP indemnity, carries all three customary exclusions (Licensee modifications, combinations with items not supplied by Licensor, Licensee specifications), imposes mandatory procure/modify/replace remedies with a refund fallback, and caps that indemnity at three times annual fees paid. The two consequential edits to Article XIII are necessary, not extras: XIII(a) expressly barred any Licensor liability for infringement claims and XIII(b) capped Licensor at one half of amounts paid, either of which would have rendered the new indemnity and its 3x super-cap illusory. Each carve-out is drafted narrowly ("EXCEPT FOR LICENSOR'S INDEMNITY OBLIGATIONS UNDER ARTICLE XII-A") and no existing wording is deleted, so minimality holds. No preferred-level content was smuggled in (no defence duty, affiliates, breach-of-law, data-breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct limbs, no notice/control/cooperation procedure, no narrowing of Article XII), and no survival tail, expense or damages boilerplate was added — consistent with a clean fallback-only proposal. Preferred level is not reached and the finding should not be characterised as such: to move up, the drafter would need to add "defend, indemnify and hold harmless Licensee and its affiliates", limbs for Licensor's breach of applicable law, Licensor-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of Licensee data, and Licensor's gross negligence/wilful misconduct, a notice/control/cooperation procedure, corresponding widening of the Article XIII(a) and (b) carve-outs beyond Article XII-A's IP-only scope, and a narrowing of Article XII to Licensee-provided content and Licensee's breach of law. Residual tension to watch (not a defect in the selected checklist): retained Article XII still makes Licensee "solely responsible for any commercial or legal liability that may arise as a result of Licensee's exercise of any of the license rights", which could be argued to circle back an infringement claim Licensor has just indemnified. A one-line opener to Article XII — "Except as provided in Article XII-A," — would remove the argument without expanding scope. Severity remains critical as a finding: the unamended Agreement sits in walk-away territory (one-way Licensee indemnity plus an express bar on any Licensor infringement liability and a half-of-fees cap); the proposed language cures it to the fallback.

rationale: Article III (p0048) vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein in Licensor, and "DERIVATIVE WORK" (p0005) sweeps in any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements. The customization work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) (p0087) — a unique client front end and other enhancements to the Platform Software — therefore vests entirely in Licensor, while our only right is the non-exclusive Field-of-Use licence that may not be copied, modified or sublicensed (p0042, p0044, p0047, p0048, p0085) and that terminates automatically under Article XXI(a) with a five-day ship-back and officer certification under Article XXI(b) (p0138). That fails the IP fallback: we receive no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense what we paid for. Licensor's retained ownership of its platform, tools and know-how is acceptable and is left untouched, as are its infringement-enforcement rights, the Article VII(b) pricing mechanic and the balance of Article XXI. No Customer IP or data is assigned to Licensor and there is no standing Licensor licence in our data, so we simply confine any such licence to processing to provide the services. We drafted to the fallback rather than the preferred level (no assignment of the customizations to us and no affirmative data-ownership sentence) to avoid collateral rewrites of Articles II, III, VI and XXI; the named override of Article III and Article XXI(a) and (b) is the minimum needed to keep the perpetual licence from being cancelled or surrendered.

verification.notes: Position-complete at the fallback level: all eight fallback elements are met by the inserted CUSTOMIZATION DELIVERABLES paragraph, which is scoped to the Article VII(b) work — the only deliverable/work product created for Licensee under this Agreement. Preferred level fails on two operative gaps the drafter would have to repair if escalating: (i) no sentence vesting or assigning ownership of the Article VII(b) customization work (and the Derivative Works it constitutes) in Licensee, and (ii) no affirmative sentence retaining Licensee's right, title and interest in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee — the data sentence only caps Licensor's licence and ownership cannot be inferred from it. Minimality holds: nothing is deleted, Article III's Licensor-favourable retained ownership, its infringement-enforcement rights, the Article VII(b) pricing mechanic and the balance of Article XXI survive. The notwithstanding override is not a blanket 'anything to the contrary' clause — it names Articles II, III, VI and XXI(a)/(b) only, and each is genuinely necessary (Articles II/III/VI to unlock use, modification, copying and sublicensing; XXI(a)/(b) to prevent automatic licence termination and ship-back from defeating the perpetual/irrevocable elements). No survival tail, expense allocation, procedure or extra damages category is added. Minor drafting note, not a minimality failure: the defined term "Customization Deliverables" is created but never used again; it could be dropped without loss. Intent is preserved: no dangling cross-reference or undefined trigger is introduced (Article VII(b) remains the commissioning mechanic, and the licence simply attaches to work actually performed under it), and the named overrides prevent the retained Article XXI sentences from contradicting the new grant. Finding classification of 'deviation' is correct — the pre-redline clause failed the fallback outright (no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free use/modify/sublicense licence to what Licensee pays for, and the licence terminated automatically under Article XXI(a)).

verification.notes: Fallback level is complete: the cap in (b) is now bilateral and set at fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim, and a single appended sentence lifts indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct out of the cap for each party. Preferred level fails on five points the drafter should note if pushing higher: no "paid or payable" wording, no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor, no data-protection/security, fraud or IP-infringement carve-outs, and no statement that Licensee's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. The rationale's justification for leaving Section (a) alone is wrong on the facts: "IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE ... FOR ANY SPECIAL, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES" protects the Vendor only and leaves Licensee exposed to consequential-damages claims; the asymmetry is adverse, not favourable. This does not defeat the fallback (which omits the exclusion element), but the comment should not assert a Customer benefit that does not exist. Retained (a) still absolutely excludes Licensor liability for IP-infringement claims arising from use of the Licensed Technology, which sits directly against the preferred IP carve-out; flag it if the preferred position is pursued. Because the cap is now mutual with no payment carve-out, consider adding "Licensee's obligation to pay fees due hereunder is not subject to this cap" only if pursuing preferred — it is outside the fallback checklist and its omission is correctly not treated as a defect here. Minimality holds: two surgical operations, no survival tail, no added procedures, no deletion of favourable retained language ((c) and the (a) exclusion remain intact), and the carve-out list matches the fallback checklist exactly. Intent is preserved: the added sentence cross-refers to an existing "SECTION (b)", introduces no undefined terms, and does not contradict the retained material-inducement statement in (c).
